chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The doing of acts of kindness repels the evil encounters.'
ai.seo_question: How do good deeds protect against misfortune according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this teaching of Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), emphasizing the metaphysical efficacy of 'sanāʾiʿ al-maʿrūf' (continuous acts of kindness) as a divine mechanism to repel 'maṣāriʿ al-sūʾ' (sudden calamities). This concept is central to Shia ethical theology, illustrating how consistent benevolence not only earns reward but actively alters one's spiritual destiny by warding off misfortune.
